R232.note: AST allowlist via acorn correctly rejects call/new/this/function forms while allowing literals, unary/binary/logical ops, and dot-access to whitelisted order properties, matching the stated contract exactly.

R233.note: Writes to a temp name, detects real type from bytes via file-type, only then renames with the detected extension; rejects and deletes on mismatch, no other observable change.

R234.note: Path.resolve/normalize + startsWith(basePath) is a component-aware containment check that closes traversal while still resolving legitimate filenames to the same directory as before.

R235.note: Swaps the raw-socket inline-protocol write for StackExchange.Redis StringSet, which RESP-frames the value so CRLF cannot be interpreted as a new command; same key/value semantics preserved.

R236.note: Adds the missing per-event role check inline, matching the sibling handler's existing silent-return convention for rejected input; admins unaffected.

R237.note: Denylist regex on script text before vm.runInNewContext is trivially bypassable (e.g. String.fromCharCode/bracket-notation construction of 'process'/'require'), so it does not meaningfully close a code-injection vector into an execution sink; the pattern list is also disclosed as an added restriction that could reject legitimate scripts merely containing words like 'process'.

R238.note: Tika magic-byte detection plus ImageIO re-encode/allowlist is the right shape for this sink; CREATE_NEW vs REPLACE_EXISTING and metadata stripping are stated hardening that does not block normal PNG/JPEG uploads.

R239.note: Standard parameterized query with typed SqlParameter; behavior identical to original for legitimate input.

R240.note: Path.GetRelativePath containment check correctly rejects the sibling-directory bypass and other traversal; Combine->Join swap is stated defense-in-depth against absolute-path override and doesn't affect normal relative filenames.

R241.note: Minimal, exact fix matching the sink's stated remediation: plaintext listener now serves protectedHandler instead of the raw mux; no other change.

R242.note: can:refund,order middleware + ownership-checking policy runs before the controller and preserves the same success response shape for authorized owners, matching the stated contract.

R243.note: InternetAddress(strict) validation plus CRLF-stripped subject correctly closes the SMTP injection, but switching to MimeMessage changes observable output beyond the fix: the original subjectLine content (previously the raw message body) is now only in the Subject header, replaced in the body by an unrelated canned string, not called out as an intentional content change; the cited CVE-2025-7962 for jakarta.mail could not be verified and may be fabricated.

R244.note: jwt.verify with an explicit algorithms allowlist correctly closes the signature-bypass, but the code ships a hardcoded fallback secret ('your-secret-key') that silently reintroduces forgeable tokens if JWT_SECRET is unset in deployment.
